fields.description:
## Context / Problem
`make worktree name=<branch>` creates the branch/worktree, but if its delegated `make venv && make install` step fails, the recipe continues, prints "✓ worktree ready," and exits 0.

Observed when an ambient `uv` violated the repository's pinned expectation: `make venv` failed and no `.venv` existed, yet the target reported success. The agent then works in a worktree with no `ruff`/`mypy`, and the pre-commit gate fails at commit time with `make: mypy: No such file or directory` — which reads as a code problem rather than an environment one.

This is the "absence of execution reported as success" defect class: provisioning did not happen, and the exit status said it did.

## Root cause
`Makefile:198` `worktree:` executes its provisioning as a single shell line whose commands are joined with `;`, and make does **not** apply `set -e` semantics inside a recipe line (make only checks the exit status of the whole line, i.e. of the last command in the list). Verified in the tree at `Makefile` lines 211-220:

```
	git fetch origin; \
	git worktree add "$$target_dir" -b "$(name)" origin/main; \
	( cd "$$target_dir" && $(MAKE) venv && . .venv/bin/activate && $(MAKE) install ); \
	echo ""; \
	echo "✓ worktree ready: $$target_dir"; \
```

The provisioning subshell's non-zero status is discarded by the following `;`, and the line's status becomes that of the final `echo` — zero. The sibling `venv:` target (`Makefile` lines 188-196) already gets this right by using `|| { …; exit 1; }` explicitly, so the fix is to bring `worktree:` to the same standard.

## Approach
Make the `worktree:` recipe line fail-fast and make each failure name itself:

1. Prefix the recipe line with `set -e` so every command in the list aborts the line (portable POSIX-shell behaviour; make runs recipes under `/bin/sh` by default, so this needs no GNU-only feature and no CI provider).
2. Wrap each of the three fallible steps — `git fetch origin`, `git worktree add`, and the provisioning subshell — in an explicit `|| { echo "ERROR: …"; exit 1; }` that names the step that failed and (for provisioning) tells the reader the worktree exists but is unprovisioned and how to finish or remove it. The explicit handlers are what makes the failure loud; `set -e` is the belt-and-braces that catches anything added later without a handler.
3. The `✓ worktree ready` message stays where it is; because the line now aborts, it is only reachable after provisioning succeeds.

Chosen over restructuring the target into separate recipe lines (one per step, letting make's own per-line status checking do the work) because the recipe carries a shell variable `target_dir` across all its steps; make runs each recipe line in its own shell, so splitting would require recomputing or exporting that variable in every line — more moving parts for the same guarantee.

## Scope
- `Makefile` — the `worktree:` target only (`set -e` + per-step error handlers). No other target changes.
- `tests/unit/test_makefile_worktree.py` — new regression test.

## Testing
The regression test drives the **real** `Makefile` in a throwaway `tmp_path` sandbox, following the sandbox pattern already used by `tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py::_sandbox` (which copies the Makefile into `tmp_path` and prepends a stub-bin directory to `PATH`). Two stubs isolate the recipe's control flow from the host: a stub `git` on `PATH` (recording, and creating the target directory on `worktree add`), and the delegated provisioning stubbed by passing `MAKE=<stub>` as a command-line variable, which overrides the `$(MAKE)` the recipe expands. The stub `make` records its argument and exits with a caller-chosen status, and on a successful `venv` creates a `.venv/bin/activate` so the recipe's `.` sourcing step behaves. No real worktree, branch, network fetch, venv, or `uv`/`pre-commit` invocation happens, so the tests are subprocess-fast and leave nothing on the host.

- Failure path (the bug): `git` stubbed to succeed, provisioning stubbed to fail. Assert `make worktree` exits non-zero, that its combined output does **not** contain the `✓ worktree ready` success message, and that it does contain an `ERROR:` line naming provisioning.
- Failure path (earlier step): `git worktree add` stubbed to exit non-zero. Assert non-zero exit and no success message.
- Happy path: every stub succeeds. Assert exit 0 and that the success message is printed — so the fix cannot be "always fail".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With provisioning stubbed to fail, `make worktree name=<x> dir=<tmp>` exits non-zero — verified by the new test asserting `returncode != 0`.
- [ ] In that same failing run the string `✓ worktree ready` is absent from stdout+stderr, and an `ERROR:` line naming the failed step is present — verified by the new test's output assertions.
- [ ] With `git worktree add` stubbed to fail, `make worktree` exits non-zero — verified by the new test.
- [ ] With every step stubbed to succeed, `make worktree` still exits 0 and prints the success message — verified by the new test.
- [ ] The regression test creates no real worktree, branch, or venv outside its sandbox — verified by the test running entirely under `tmp_path` with a stub `git` on `PATH` and a stubbed `$(MAKE)`, so no `git worktree add`, `uv`, or network call reaches the host.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0.
